$comment: About and Contact. One file per language, the same shape as content/pages. A language without a file falls back to nothing: the build skips it and the sitemap does not claim it. Unlike the guides, these two carry no lead. They keep headings, but few: About is why it exists and who created and maintains it, Contact is bugs and security, and the meta about response times comes before either. A page of one-paragraph subsections read as a brochure rather than as a person.

about.title: About Lukotta
about.description: Why Lukotta exists, what it is built on, and who created and maintains it. A Mac app for BitLocker and Linux drives, still in early development.

sections.heading: Why it exists
paragraphs: I wanted backups from a Windows PC and a Mac on the same external disk. The Mac could not open the BitLocker volume, and the existing ways of doing it were more complicated than they needed to be.
Lukotta is built on [anylinuxfs](https://github.com/nohajc/anylinuxfs), which opens the drive inside a small Linux virtual machine and hands it back to macOS.
anylinuxfs is a command-line tool, which rules it out for most people. There are graphical wrappers for tools like it, but they look and feel like an aeroplane cockpit.
Lukotta's main goal is perfect user experience: plug in the drive, type the password, open it in Finder. A drive should be fully usable on any computer.

sections.heading: Who created and maintains it
paragraphs: Lukotta is being developed by [one person](https://rahula.dev). I have spent years in software engineering and UX design, so the interface gets as much attention as the code underneath. Working alone is also more practical than it used to be, because AI-assisted development handles the repetitive work.
Lukotta is not finished. There is interface work still to do and bugs to fix, some of them in the tools it depends on. Reading drives is reliable; writing to them is still experimental.

contact.title: Contact
contact.description: How to report a bug in Lukotta, suggest a change or correct a translation, and where security problems go. The issue tracker on GitHub is fastest.

paragraphs: Please tell me about anything that is broken, confusing or missing.
Lukotta is a one-person project, so there is no guaranteed response time. I read everything and answer within a few days.

sections.heading: Bugs, suggestions and translations
paragraphs: Please use the issue tracker at github.com/clementrahula/lukotta/issues. If you have not used GitHub before, it is the site that hosts Lukotta's source code, and an issue is a public message about the project. Writing one requires a free account. Issues are the first thing I read, and they stay public for the next person with the same question.
For a bug, describe the drive, what Lukotta showed you and what you expected, and quote any error message exactly. Do not include a password or a recovery key.
Corrections to the translations are just as useful. I do not speak most of the languages the app is published in, so please quote the line and say what it should be instead.
You can also email contact_web@lukotta.com if you would rather not use GitHub, though I reply to email more slowly.

sections.heading: Security problems
paragraphs: Please do not report a security problem in a public issue. Use the advisory form at github.com/clementrahula/lukotta/security/advisories/new.
